task.description: REQ-VALIDATOR gate over REQ-114, REQ-115, REQ-116, REQ-117. Apply your role's whole checklist: every criterion checkable by the named test or command and not by a person's taste; no criterion weaker than PLAN's acceptance lines and audit chapter 10 for the same thing (name each one compared); no production check as a criterion; no contradiction with another block, ARCH, a plan amendment or the ORCH answers; the owner's words quoted verbatim where relied on; the goal of decisions/0133 served and nothing outside it added; dependencies and order named; no secret, machine path or reference-product name. Re-derive at least three claims of the analyst's self_check yourself (for example the unchanged rest of the file by hash against HEAD~1 or the commit named in the handoff, a test file that a criterion says exists, a number). Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings by severity (blocking / non-blocking), each with the block, the criterion number, the problem and the exact change you want. Be economical. RULES OF THIS PC (decisions/0110, 0127, 0129): do NOT run npm run check, cd app && npm run ..., node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; the record of a test run is read from GitHub with gh run view (read-only). Allowed: cd tools && npm run -s traces and handoffs-check; read-only git and gh; your own scripts and fresh clones (git clone -c core.autocrlf=false, npm ci) only in your own folder under <scratch> (the real path is in the message that launched you). Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). Fill only the result of your handoff; the top-level status stays PENDING and completed_at null: ORCH closes. English.

findings.problem: Criterion 4 puts every non-GET route of the real route table under «foreign or missing Origin → 403, Content-Type other than application/json → 415». The table already holds the released public route POST /api/demo/result (app/server/routes/demo.js line 255; REQ-111 c7, done). Its tests call it without Origin and without Content-Type json: app/test/int/demo.test.js `post()` (line 204, used at lines 315, 458, 528 and more), app/test/e2e/landing.test.js line 1838 (fetch POST with a string body, no headers); app/test/int/demo-parity.test.js and app/test/e2e/stage.test.js also call the route. They turn red, yet no row (1)-(7) of the guard table names them and criterion 14 says no other test changes. The same criterion will also reach the worker routes of lane B (/api/worker/*, a token, no browser Origin) when they join the table.
findings.fix: State in the description and in criterion 4 which routes the browser CSRF/Origin/Content-Type rule covers (for example by a metadata key, with the public demo route and the worker routes named as outside it and why), or, if the demo route is to be covered, add guard rows for demo.test.js, demo-parity.test.js, landing.test.js and stage.test.js and say how the released REQ-111 behaviour changes.

findings.problem: «for every route of the table, a query parameter org_id and a header x-sai-org … change nothing in the answer (the same status and body as without them)» cannot hold for routes whose answer carries fresh values or that are single-use: POST /api/admin/invites (a new code), POST /api/auth/reauth (a new token), POST /api/projects (a new id), POST /api/auth/setup (the second call is 404), POST /api/auth/login (the counters move). A literal test is red on correct code, so step 9 cannot answer yes.
findings.fix: Give a comparison that can be met: e.g. the same status and the same body after masking the generated fields the code design lists, and for a route that creates a row, the org_id of that row equals the session's organisation; or bound the body-equality part to the read routes and add the row check for the writing routes.
